tasks.title: Revoke refresh tokens and reset credentials
tasks.description: Revoke active sessions for the affected accounts and force password resets.

logs.message: Revoked all active refresh tokens and forced a credential reset for the three accounts via `Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken`. Sessions killed across web and mobile.
Verified **no active sessions** remain and users re-authenticated cleanly. Task complete — *phishing-resistant MFA re-enrolment* tracked separately under the Recover task.

tasks.title: Remove mailbox rules and check forwarding
tasks.description:
**Objective:** find and remove attacker-created inbox rules and forwarding on the
three affected mailboxes, then confirm none remain.

### Steps

1. Export inbox rules with `Get-InboxRule` for each mailbox.
2. Check forwarding (`ForwardingSMTPAddress`, `ForwardingAddress`).
3. Remove malicious rules and capture each as evidence.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three mailboxes audited
- [ ] Malicious rules removed and screenshotted
- [ ] Forwarding confirmed disabled

See the [BEC investigation guide](/knowledge-base) for the full rule-abuse checklist.

logs.message:
Pulled inbox rules for all three mailboxes. Found a malicious rule on
`svc-billing`:

| Rule | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `.` (single-dot match) | Move to **RSS Feeds**, mark as read |

Rule **deleted** and exported as evidence. Forwarding was clean on the two user
mailboxes.

Re-ran `Get-InboxRule` after the deletion — *no* residual rules remain. Mailbox
side is done; the shared-account forwarding audit is still **pending**.

tasks.title: User comms + phishing-resistant MFA enrolment
tasks.description:
**Objective:** notify affected users and re-enrol them onto phishing-resistant MFA.

- Send the templated compromise notice to each user **and** their manager.
- Walk users through FIDO2 / passkey enrolment.
- Revoke legacy MFA methods (*SMS*, *voice*) once passkeys are active.

> Do not re-trust the old phone numbers — the lure harvested them.

tasks.description:

Keep it *non-technical* and link the full timeline in the case.

tasks.title: Isolate affected hosts from network
tasks.description: Network-contain SRV-APP01 and all workstations with C2 callbacks.

logs.message:
Network-contained the hosts showing C2 callbacks. Actions taken:

| Host | Action | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SRV-APP01` | EDR network-contain | Isolated |
| `WKS-2210` | EDR network-contain | Isolated |
| Finance VLAN | ACL deny to `45.155.205.233` | Blocked |
Containment **verified** — no further beaconing observed for 10+ minutes. Hosts left powered on for memory capture (see the forensics task).

tasks.description: Add 45.155.205.233 and associated domains to blocklist on perimeter firewalls.

tasks.title: Identify ransomware family and variant
tasks.description:
**Objective:** identify the ransomware family / variant from the staged binaries.

### Indicators to check

| Artefact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Staged binary | `p64.exe` in `C:\PerfLogs\` |
| File marker | `.0rgn` extension |
| C2 | `45.155.205.233` |

- Submit hashes to the malware sandbox and **MISP**.
- Match observed TTPs against known families.

> Priority: confirm whether this is a *known* family with a public decryptor
> **before** recovery planning.

logs.message:
Submitted the staged binary to the sandbox and **MISP**.

- **SHA-256:** `9b2c…f41a`
- Sandbox verdict: *Cobalt Strike loader* (stager, not a locker yet)
- No public decryptor — treat as **no-decrypt** for recovery planning.

tasks.title: Snapshot affected hypervisor cluster
tasks.description:
**Objective:** snapshot the affected hypervisor cluster before any remediation.

1. Quiesce and snapshot each guest on the impacted hosts.
2. Preserve snapshots *read-only* for forensics.
3. Do **not** power off — capture RAM first.

tasks.title: Pull EDR timeline for initial access
tasks.description:
**Objective:** reconstruct the initial-access → lateral-movement timeline from EDR.

- Pull the process tree on `SRV-APP01` back to patient zero.
- Map every `PsExec` execution to its target host.
- Tag each step to MITRE ATT&CK —
  [T1570](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1570/) /
  [T1486](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/).

logs.message:
Initial access traced to a phishing attachment opened on `WKS-2210` at **09:14**,
followed by `PsExec` to `SRV-APP01` at **09:22**. Full process tree attached to
the case; ATT&CK mapping in progress.
